title: She Told the World She's Pregnant. Two Days Later, She Showed Up to Fight Shah Rukh Khan.
excerpt: Deepika Padukone is juggling two of 2026's biggest films — King and Raka — while expecting her second child. Neither character has been trimmed. Neither film has slowed down.
body:
Forty-eight hours.

That's how long Deepika Padukone waited after announcing her second pregnancy before showing up at Golden Tobacco Studio in Vile Parle, Mumbai, ready to throw punches. On April 21 and 22, barely two days after telling the world she and Ranveer Singh are expecting again, she filmed an intense two-day combat sequence for King — the kind where she and Shah Rukh Khan take on eight fighters in a single, highly stylised scene that trade sources describe as "a visual treat for action aficionados."

If that sounds like a flex, it's because it is.

Two Films, ₹450 Crore, Zero Compromises

The numbers behind Deepika's current calendar are staggering. King, directed by Siddharth Anand, carries a reported budget of ₹350 crore and a December 24 release date — Christmas Day, the most coveted slot on the Bollywood calendar. Its cast reads like a greatest-hits compilation of Hindi cinema: SRK, Suhana Khan making her theatrical debut alongside her father, Abhishek Bachchan, Anil Kapoor, Jackie Shroff, Rani Mukerji, Jaideep Ahlawat, and the gravity-defying Raghav Juyal. The score is by Anirudh Ravichander. The screenplay by Sujoy Ghosh. This is not a film that does anything small.

> "Her character is described as a key protagonist with a "stellar entry sequence" and a major action-packed moment opposite Allu Arjun."

And Deepika isn't a supporting player — she's in the thick of the action, matching SRK blow for blow.

Then there's Raka. Atlee's follow-up to the ₹1,000-crore juggernaut *Jawan*, headlined by Allu Arjun, still has approximately 50 days of shooting remaining on Deepika's schedule. Her character is described as a key protagonist with a "stellar entry sequence" and a major action-packed moment opposite Allu Arjun. When Atlee heard the pregnancy news, he reportedly sat down with his creative team the same day to build a Plan B: a body double for the physically demanding stunt work, with Deepika's close-ups filmed separately and integrated through VFX in post-production.

![Mumbai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/2b/Mumbai_Bandra-Worli_Sea_Link.jpg)

What's remarkable is what *didn't* happen. Her character in King stays fully intact — no deletions, no rewrites, no convenient offscreen exit. The same goes for Raka. Two of the year's most expensive productions adjusted their entire shooting schedules around her. She didn't adjust herself around them.

Cape Town, Mira Road, and a Race Against Time

The production blueprint for King has been meticulously calibrated around Deepika's pregnancy timeline. After the Mumbai leg — which included that now-famous Golden Tobacco fight shoot — she is set to join the international unit in South Africa for a crucial climax setpiece lasting about a week. Then it's back to Mumbai, where Siddharth Anand has planned an elaborate sequence involving a massive sandy backdrop at a specialised studio in Mira Road.

The goal: wrap all major climactic sequences involving Deepika by mid-production, well before her pregnancy advances. Several close-up sequences have already been filmed and will be composited with stunt footage using advanced VFX — so the action stays uncompromised while the expectant mother focuses on the dramatic beats of her role. King's principal photography is expected to wrap entirely by September 2026.

The Bigger Picture

Here's the part the industry is still processing: Deepika Padukone is simultaneously the female lead in films starring Shah Rukh Khan and Allu Arjun — arguably the two biggest male stars in Indian cinema right now, one commanding the Hindi belt, the other ruling the South. She is the connective tissue between a ₹350-crore Bollywood tentpole releasing on Christmas and a mega-budget pan-India action spectacle from the director who turned SRK into a box-office force of nature all over again.

Her last theatrical release, *Kalki 2898 AD*, sailed past the ₹1,000-crore mark worldwide. Before that, *Pathaan* and *Jawan* — both with SRK — redefined what Hindi cinema could earn. Deepika doesn't just pick the biggest films; she *is* the reason they get that big.

For diaspora audiences watching from North America, the UK, and the Gulf, King arrives December 24 — expect IMAX and premium format releases globally. Raka's release date remains under wraps, but with Atlee and Allu Arjun's staggering international pull, worldwide distribution is a certainty. Both films will stream with Hindi, Telugu, and Tamil audio options.

There's no body-double for that kind of star power.
